inlines.v: SCOUT, noun [Latin ausculto, culto, colo; Gr. the ear.] 1. In military affairs, a person sent before an army, or to a distance, for the purpose of observing the motions of an enemy or discovering any danger, and giving notice to the general. Horsemen are generally employed as scouts. 2. A high rock. [Not in use.] SCOUT, verb intransitive To go on the business of watching the motions of an enemy; to act as a scout With obscure wing scout far and wide into the realm of night. SCOUT, verb transitive To sneer at; to treat with disdain and contempt. [This word is in good use in America.]
